instruction: Change the permission of all regular files under current directory tree to 777

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.write('cd testDir'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.write('clear'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all regular files to 777 permissions (-rwxrwxrwx). Evaluator checks that all files in testDir have the correct permission string.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical directory context mismatch: Setup navigates INTO testDir with 'cd testDir', but evaluator command uses 'find testDir' which will fail
After setup completes, working directory is testDir. Running 'find testDir' from inside testDir looks for testDir/testDir which doesn't exist
The evaluator will return no results or error, causing verification to fail even if permissions were correctly changed
Metric logic is correct: properly parses ls -l output and checks all files have -rwxrwxrwx permission
Command structure would work if directory context was correct
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change evaluator command from 'find testDir -type f -exec ls -l {} \;' to 'find . -type f -exec ls -l {} \;' to search current directory
OR remove 'cd testDir' from setup config so evaluation runs from parent directory
OR add absolute path handling by using 'cd ~ && find testDir -type f -exec ls -l {} \;' in evaluator
